rect.title: top-left logic: random logic
bottom-centre logic: random logic below the central datapath
top-right bus field: horizontal buses under the test structures
left bus field: dense horizontal wiring between the left array and the rest
bottom bus field: wiring along the bottom of the core
top-centre logic: random logic left of the central datapath
left-centre logic: random logic between the left array and the central datapath
bus field (datapath to counters): about twenty vertical metal lines; an eight-line bus joins the central datapath's rows at y 10345-10650 and y 13300-13620. Surveyed, not traced

horizontal counter (8 bit): synchronous two-phase counter; the horizontal character counter: its master outputs are the c lines of the R0, R1 and R2 comparators (bit 0 = bottom row r18). Clocked by ck_b (master) and ck_a (slave) every cycle; carry enters at r18 and ripples up, with a 4-bit look-ahead line (group line B)
bottom-left logic: random logic near DISPTMG/CUDISP pads
MA line bundle: nine vertical metal tracks between the left column and the MA output drivers; lines step from track to track

character row counter (7 bit): synchronous two-phase counter; the character-row counter: its outputs go to the R4 and R6 comparators of the upper right array. Its two clocks are NOT ck_a/ck_b but two lines from the logic to the west (bus lines D and E), so it steps only when that logic pulses them; carry enters at r10, 4-bit look-ahead line (group line A)

left column beside the arrays: cells on the row boundaries; the inputs of the MA8 and MA9 output drivers end in the cells at the s4/s5 and s8/s9 boundaries (traced), so these are the MA output stages; group carry logic believed here too. Cells not traced

MA counter: incrementer and bit (14 rows): per row: carry = carry-in AND Q, sum = carry-in XOR Q by pass gates, all-ones line per group; the bit is a static pair with a weak hold device. Believed the MA counter. Traced

svg.text: MA counter: incrementer and bit (14 rows)

rect.title: bundle line 3 (r9m_l3): from the step logic's track P (lower piece) up x 4194, east along y 2641, down a step to y 2681, east and south along x 5848 to (5845,5045)
RA0, RA1 driver input lines: from the pad cells down to their polys at x 15303 / 15345
process test structures: devices labelled E, A, S, D with probe pads
top-right logic rows: gates under the test structures, near the RA/HSYNC/VSYNC pads (the RA output stage below is ral)
RA2 driver input: south along x 17727 and west along y 3878
MA row cells, right column: one cell per counter row; not looked at
MA output stages (14 ral cells): the ral cell turned 90 degrees, once per MA bit; strobed by ck_out (the left-edge trunk); believed a latch per bit (partly traced)
die marking: HD46505S and mask revision marks
scan line counter (5 bit): five copies of the counter bit cell (sl4..sl0 from the top), a plain ripple chain; stepped once per pulse of lc_step; compared with R5 in the upper right datapath

MA counter latch stage: dynamic node X1 takes the incremented value (strobe Vm2) or a value from the right (Vm3); inverter; pass gate to Y (Vm5); write gate of the stored bit (Vm6); clear (Vm1). Traced

wiring channel right of the counters: seven metal tracks with poly hidden under them: write strobes of R3, R5, R6, R7 going north, the counter outputs going east to the comparators (rows r4-r14) or north (r0-r3), match lines coming back, and the clock-related line inh_rc on its way to the top of the array

svg.text: wiring channel right of the counters

rect.title: 4-bit counter (left array): four copies of the counter bit cell of the mid-right array (c4l3..c4l0 from the top); shares its master and slave clock with the 5-bit counter below; not yet identified
horizontal sync width counter (4 bit): rows r0-r3; on the character clock like the horizontal counter; compared with R3's nibble in the upper right datapath
MA counter rows, middle (untraced): Y ends on a gate here, Z (the value written back) and the load value come from here; a wide driver on rail F. Not traced

routing zone above R7: the four lines of the horizontal sync width counter and the five of the scan line counter arrive here from the west and end under the comparators' counter tracks; R3's data lines leave east

counter outputs of the left array: nine tracks: the 4-bit counter's outputs go north to four poly lines east along y 6157-6280; the 5-bit counter's step east and go north to five poly lines along y 6498-6673, which run 9,000 px east through the central datapath's channel 2 to the upper right datapath

svg.text: counter outputs of the left array

rect.title: register address decode (18 selects): NOR array, 5-bit address to 18 register selects. Columns left to right select R7 R6 R4 R0 R2 R1 R10 R5 R3 R8 R9 R11 R13 R12 R14 R15 R17 R16. Nothing decodes addresses 18-31
write strobes R8-R11, north: four nested metals up the central datapath's east edge, one ending on each register row's strobe
channel 2: 13 horizontal poly lines under the per-slice metal lines and rails; the lowest carries the comparator's chain output
bus and counter-line routing: poly cross-unders: bus lines s0, s5, s6, s7 leave to the lower right (s0 also goes up the right edge on x 16838); the eight c lines leave to the lower left

4-way read selector (8 bit): four pass transistors per slice put one of four sources on the output node n: a and c are 6 bits wide (slices s2-s7, the two left slices strapped to VSS), b and d 8 bits; select lines sel1-sel4 come from the left
line r9m_l1w: from a poly going north at x 5175 (not followed), east along y 2599, south along x 6022 (beside R9's line)
routing zone: horizontal poly lines; carries R0 bit 7 (y 9487) and comparator D's output (y 9532); otherwise not traced

middle cluster of the vertical control: same construction as the step logic cluster, 1042 px east: small NOR gates on a column beside a VSS rail. Three gates traced (the one that makes in1 of the step gate, an inverter, and a NOR that takes in1)

svg.text: middle cluster of the vertical control ?

rect.title: write strobes R8-R11, south: four metals down to the bottom bus
data bus, east: eight lines step down one track, then end on pads into the right datapath: db_b1-b4, R5's match
input buffers (CLK, R/W, E, RS, CS): CLK and E: three-finger inverter then two-finger inverter. R/W, RS, CS: chain of four inverters each, both polarities available. One more inverter at the left end

svg.text: input buffers (CLK, R/W, E, RS, CS)

rect.title: read gates onto bus N (rows E, F): two pass transistors per column: gate_e puts the six row C register bits (and 0 in the two left columns) on bus N, gate_f the eight row H values

svg.text: read gates onto bus N (rows E, F)

rect.title: data bus channel: fourteen poly lines; each bit line of the two registers meets one line that runs east (believed the data bus), seven lines pass through

row counter step logic (cluster): two mirrored columns of small gates between VSS, VCC, VSS rails. Traced: the row counter's step = in1 OR (NOT e4 AND NOT (e3 AND a2)) and its gates; in the west column an inverting two-way selector (y 3255-3590: one input believed the vertical sync width match) switched by the net on thin metal E, its inverter, and an inverter that drives thin metal W. About fifteen more gates not traced

left-edge bundle: twelve vertical tracks stepping one place left at y 12300-12540: write strobes wr_r0 (to R0 above), wr_r2, wr_r1, wr_r4 coming up; R2 match going north, R1 match going south; four c lines going south
channel G tracks: per column: one poly line between the west edge and the row H cell, and the column's bus N line leaving east
scan line counter lines: sl0-sl4 from the left array's wiring channel east: over the poly bus, through the central datapath's channel 2 (unused there), to the corners at x 11200-11360

channel B tracks and links: six poly lines from the west, one into each row A cell; short poly links take a second line of each row A cell onto vertical line f, which runs down through row C to the rows below
strobe track channel: 18 vertical metal tracks with poly cross-unders; wr_r5 and wr_r7 climb it from the bottom and leave north on tracks k1, k2; other lines go into the mid-right array
right-hand column (untraced): not looked at
vertical bus: seven metal positions, in pieces, joining the gate clusters at x 2450-3090 to each other and to poly lines going east. Eight pieces drawn
R0 comparator (8 bit): XOR per bit and wired NOR; output south on bundle track L2 (end of line if c is the horizontal counter)
data bits 0-3, field: four metals down dbus's wiring field to units 0-3
CLK pin to the bottom row: CLK pin node in wide poly and metal to the cell row above the CUDISP pad

svg.text: CLK pin to the bottom row

rect.title: RA3 driver input: from the RA3 pad cell south along x 17771 and west along y 3962
R3 data, bundle: four thin metals north to R3's data lines

R10 comparator (equal, greater): per bit: XOR of the register bit with the bit on the slice's through track, a chain from left (most significant) to right, and a pull-down on a row-long line. Believed outputs: "equal" at the right end of the chain, "greater" on the line; one connection per bit not seen
middle bundle (16 tracks): selects down to the gates, strobes of R10 R5 R3 R8 R9 R11 down; rsel12 rsel13 pass through; taps to the right-hand column
8-bit latch (selector source b): the register latch cell upside down: strobe line along its bottom edge, data tracks from the row above, buffered output down to the selector

8-bit read/write register (row H): the row C register cell upside down in all eight columns, on the same bit lines, with its own write line; outputs west on the channel G tracks and onto bus N. Believed R13 or R15 (low byte)
rows D and E (5 cells): not traced
channel 2: latch data in, selector out: per slice one poly line in two pieces: from the left edge to the latch input, and from the selector node n to the right edge (towards the data bus)

svg.text: channel 2: latch data in, selector out

rect.title: 8-bit latch (selector source d): pass transistor loaded from the left by strobe ld, two inverters, and a buffer inverter that drives the selector; same cell family as the right datapath's register latch
R4 comparator (7 bit): XOR per bit and wired NOR against the upper array's seven c lines (believed the row counter); output leaves west at y 8339
data bus, west: twelve metal lines; amr's six outputs land on six of them
R0/2 comparator (7 bit): c of each slice against the R0 bit of the next slice, bit 7 of c not compared (believed c = R0/2, the interlace half line); output south on bundle track L0
input protection (CLK, R/W, E, RS, CS): five clamp cells in order CLK, R/W, E, RS, CS; each pad reaches its cell through a resistive strip

svg.text: input protection (CLK, R/W, E, RS, CS)

rect.title: R7 comparator (7 bit): counter lines of the upper array against R7 (vertical sync position); result rc_eq_r7 leaves west
R6 comparator (7 bit): counter lines of the upper array against R6 (vertical displayed); result rc_eq_r6 goes down the wiring channel to the strobe channel
right cluster of the vertical control: not traced; one input of the step logic comes from here on a poly at y 3805

svg.text: right cluster of the vertical control ?

rect.title: clock wiring: lines A, B, their re-buffered copies, buffered CLK and the CLK pin node on their way down; six small clamp devices to VCC
write strobes R0-R11: 12 x (inverter + NOR): wr_rN = rselN AND NOT strobe. Left half top to bottom R1 R2 R0 R4 R6 R7, right half R10 R5 R3 R8 R9 R11
channel 1: per-slice lines to the left: eight poly lines from the left edge, one per slice, each tapped by a vertical metal that goes up into the row above

svg.text: channel 1: per-slice lines to the left

rect.title: R9 match line, north: north along x 5974

6-bit latch (selector source c): six latch cells under slices s1-s6, strobe from a contact at the left end, data tracks leave the bottom of the array; each buffered output is linked in poly to the c track of the next slice to the right
row of large cells (untraced): six slices, continues below y 8450 (cdp3's row A); fed by the data bus lines only from above. Not traced

R10 register (7 bit): seven copies of the same static latch cell with their own strobe line. Five bits feed the comparator above, the two leftmost bits leave to the left. Which register: not yet established (the 5 + 2 split would fit R10)
R9 compare lines, east: the units' outputs north and west, under two rails at x 16382-16550
second bus field: seven vertical metal positions, in pieces, between the middle and right clusters; five pieces drawn
R2 register (8 bit): written from the bus lines when wr_r2 is high (strobe followed down the bundle, which steps one track left at y 12357, to bd1's wr_r2)
amr lines north: six polys under the supply metal from the slices' top contacts (y 5585) to pads on the bus: data bits in, compared bits in
top bus field: seven horizontal metal lines crossing the VSS rail in poly; y 2771 = w1/ns1, y 2727 = ns2 traced, rest not
data bus bits 4-0 through rows D/E: cdp1's five slice bit lines down to R11 and R10; a 54 px necked stretch at y 5542-5596 is assumed continuous

svg.text: data bus bits 4-0 through rows D/E

rect.title: R0 register (8 bit): horizontal total; latches loaded from the data lines by wr_r0; feeds the two comparators above
row C register outputs going west: six poly lines, one from each row C cell (true data, buffered) to the west edge

svg.text: row C register outputs going west

rect.title: R1 register (8 bit): same latch cell as the address register, upside down; written from the bus lines when wr_r1 is high (strobe followed down bundle track L11, jog to L10 at y 14000, to bd1's wr_r1)

6-bit read/write register (row C): static register cell per column c2..c7: written from the column bit line when the write line is high, held through a grounded-gate device; one buffered output west, one onto bus N. Believed R12 or R14 (high bits)
R2 comparator, XOR row: per slice x = c XOR q of the R2 bit and the per-slice line c
RA output stage (5 cells): rax_o0-4 in through a pass transistor on the strobe y 4548, out to the RA drivers; a pull-down per cell on the line y 4350; believed a latch per bit (partly traced)
R1 comparator, XOR row: per slice x = c XOR q (two gates, 7 transistors) of the R1 bit and the per-slice line c
two-phase clock generator: two cross-coupled NOR drivers: ck_a (high only while CLK low) on the left, ck_b (high only while CLK high) on the right, with an inverter for NOT CLK in the middle
amr_eq_r3 to the step logic: metal x 2240 north, poly east along y 3461 into tla's first cluster (gate under rail R1 at (2625,3461))
row A cells (6 bit): large cell per column c2..c7, on the same bit lines as the two registers, with one line each from the west and one output (line f) going south; not traced
channel 3 (five control lines): five poly lines from the block west of the counters: bus line B, ck_a, the row counter's step b, band H1's line, the R2 match; no contact on the way
pad driver lines: P_x, one metal line common to all eight data pad cells (enable), and the per-bit lines and pad input lines beside it
main clock buffer: CLK pin node drives a three-stage buffer (two big inverters, then a push-pull pair). Output is NOT CLK, the main internal clock
c4l0, c4l1 north: two nested metals to the crossing field (beside bust's two for c4l2, c4l3)
R5 comparator (5 bit): scan line counter sl0-sl4 against R5 (vertical total adjust); result sl_eq_r5 leaves north
ck_out bottom trunk: NOT CLK along the bottom of the core (y 18947), from the clock block to the bottom-left corner
R7 register (7 bit): vertical sync position
R4 register (7 bit): vertical total; latches loaded by wr_r4 (strobe comes up bundle track L1); feeds the comparator above
R6 register (7 bit): vertical displayed. Same latch cells on the same data lines as R4; its strobe runs down the wiring channel to the R6 write strobe (so this is R6); its comparator is above (rdp1)

crossing field west of the datapath: horizontal poly lines over vertical metals; each of the lines ends here on one metal. The step signal b leaves north on the metal x 5841 towards the top-left logic

svg.text: crossing field west of the datapath ?

rect.title: block right of the upper rows: not surveyed

svg.text: block right of the upper rows ?

rect.title: R9 compare lines, long run: five metals along y 4005-4179
line r9m_l1w, crossing field: x 6058 poly, bus metal y 4742, poly y 4740, metal y 4744/4673 to the row y 4676, which turns south near x 8190 (not into cdp1)

comparator operand lines: five long poly lines carry a 5-bit value to the through tracks of the slices, which take it up to the rows above and down to the comparator below; the q tracks of the latch row cross them

R8 register (6 bit): six static register bits (write pass transistor, two inverters, grounded-gate feedback). Each output leaves upward on its own wire. Three bits share a bit line with the register below, three do not; R8 is believed from that and the width
R9 comparator: XOR (5 bits): per bit NOR(A,B) and an AND-OR-invert: differs = A XOR B, A the register bit, B a line from the channel below

R11 register (5 bit): five static latch bits (pass transistor from the per-slice data bus line, two inverters, weak hold device), loaded together by one strobe line. Outputs q go up to a comparator in the rows above. Which register: not yet established
data bit 5 to R10: R8 bit 5's tap down x 8727, poly west along y 6087, metal down x 8464 and 8532 to R10's second slice
scan line counter lines, east part: the five lines step up one position at x 11730-11930 and run over the logic above the counters to the R5 comparator

svg.text: scan line counter lines, east part

rect.title: R3 comparator (4 bit): horizontal sync width counter hsw0-hsw3 against R3's nibble; result hsw_eq_r3
R9 register (5 bit): five static register bits, same cell as the row above; outputs go up to the comparator. R9 by its write strobe
clock generator of the left array's counters: second copy of the row counter's generator: two non-overlapping clocks from one step pulse lc_step, which comes from the left-centre logic

svg.text: clock generator of the left array's counters

rect.title: row counter clock generator: makes the character-row counter's two non-overlapping clocks from one step pulse p: slave clock = NOR(buffered master clock, p), master clock = NOR(NOT p, buffered slave clock); two NOR drivers 350 px wide

amr_eq_r3, second crossing field: poly y 5978, metal x 3738, poly west along y 5630 to the pad (2242,5632)
address register (5 bit): five transparent latch bits loaded from bus lines s1..s5 when ar_load (ar_load) is high; outputs ar0..ar4 leave to the right
bus cross-under: cdp1's channel lines drop 65 px under the supply metal to a staircase of pads
left-edge bundle L0-L8: continues rdp3's; the two comparator outputs join it here

ck_out left-edge trunk: NOT CLK up the left edge of the left array (x 2500-2504), one metal from the bottom trunk to the pad (2500,7907) of the inverter that makes clk_tl; taps about every 608 px not looked at
R5 register (5 bit): vertical total adjust; five latches on the data lines of the array below
second crossing field: horizontal poly lines over vertical metals; the step signal b crosses it on the poly y 5585
cells right of the bundle (untraced): four identical cells then larger ones; not traced
S in the left bus field: output of input-row gate 0 (NOT X, clock-like): innermost line of the bundle, then x 6862

svg.text: S in the left bus field

rect.title: compare value (5 lines): five poly lines from the east, one per comparator bit; also the feed of one bit line of the 6-bit register from the west
D0 output fingers: three pull-up fingers (gate d0_pu) and two pull-down fingers (gate d0_pd) between the VCC rows A, E, the VSS row C and the pad rows B, D, F
D1 output fingers: three pull-up fingers (gate d1_pu) and two pull-down fingers (gate d1_pd) between the VCC rows A, E, the VSS row C and the pad rows B, D, F
D2 output fingers: three pull-up fingers (gate d2_pu) and two pull-down fingers (gate d2_pd) between the VCC rows A, E, the VSS row C and the pad rows B, D, F
D3 output fingers: three pull-up fingers (gate d3_pu) and two pull-down fingers (gate d3_pd) between the VCC rows A, E, the VSS row C and the pad rows B, D, F
D4 output fingers: three pull-up fingers (gate d4_pu) and two pull-down fingers (gate d4_pd) between the VCC rows A, E, the VSS row C and the pad rows B, D, F
D5 output fingers: three pull-up fingers (gate d5_pu) and two pull-down fingers (gate d5_pd) between the VCC rows A, E, the VSS row C and the pad rows B, D, F
D6 output fingers: three pull-up fingers (gate d6_pu) and two pull-down fingers (gate d6_pd) between the VCC rows A, E, the VSS row C and the pad rows B, D, F
D7 output fingers: three pull-up fingers (gate d7_pu) and two pull-down fingers (gate d7_pd) between the VCC rows A, E, the VSS row C and the pad rows B, D, F
left bundle: rsel7 rsel6 rsel4 rsel0 rsel2 down to their gates; strobes of R1 R2 R0 R4 R6 back up and out to the west in poly
row address lines, ends: y 4505-4722: each ends on a pad into the logic above, or goes on east
RA4 driver input: from the RA4 pad cell south along x 17771, west along y 5938, to the RA4 comparator unit's input (17335,5800)
selector output pull-down: per slice a transistor from n to VSS gated by one line (rst) from the left
select lines leave the decode array: each rselN crosses under the VSS rail in poly and continues on a metal line (or in poly) to its gate

svg.text: select lines leave the decode array

rect.title: diagonal fan: the five lines of the poly bus turn south-east and then east to pads at x 6130-6165, where horizontal metals take them on
row address lines, east: five metals along the top of the right-hand arrays to a nested corner
row address lines, north: rax_o0-4 from the east ends of the comparator lines north to the cross-under
selector outputs: the five outputs east in poly to their units; nest of metals from the units to the central datapath channel 1 lines (comparator inputs)
small cluster below the step logic: not traced; ck_out reaches it from the left-edge trunk

svg.text: small cluster below the step logic ?

rect.title: E, R/W, RS, CS to the core: e_b (metal, nested corner), rw_d / rs_d / cs_d (diagonal polys, then verticals at x 16298, 16342, 16385)

svg.text: E, R/W, RS, CS to the core

rect.title: LPSTB and RES input buffers: left cell LPSTB, right cell RES; each a small inverter then a two-finger inverter, so the core sees the pin level
gate column west of the island (untraced): about fifteen gates under one ground rail; expected to hold the field flip-flop

svg.text: gate column west of the island (untraced) ?

rect.title: R3 register (4 bit): one nibble of R3 (horizontal sync width, by the datasheet's layout); four latches with data lines of their own
R1 comparator, match line: wired NOR of the eight XORs on a row-wide diffusion line (h_eq_r1, high when R1 = c); load and exit in slice s1; leaves west in poly, then south on the bundle
ck_out feed to bottom-centre logic: two wide poly links and a metal line carry NOT CLK to the ring at 10300-10450 x 18340-18485
write strobes R8-R11, bottom: along y 17128-17258, under the vertical trunks in poly, to the strobe tracks
R9 comparator: equality NOR: one pull-down per slice on a diffusion line along the row, load in the left slice; output leaves west along y 4459. High when the register below equals the compare value
row address selector: eleven pass transistors: outputs = scan line counter, or the counter shifted up one bit with bit 0 from elsewhere
bit-0 source lines: two vertical polys under the six bus metals, then east along y 4937/4915
R3 bits 4-7 (register): four latches (columns x 11490, 11880, 12270, 12660 = data bits 4-7) written from the data bus on wr_r3; q leaves each slice south at y 6400

comparator of R3 bits 4-7: per bit: nor = NOR(c, q), x = c XOR q, against the 4-bit counter c4l0-c4l3 of the left array (through cdp1's lines l4544 / l4588 / l4632 / l4676; believed the vertical sync width counter)
2-bit decoder: two bus lines (y 14832, 14873) inverted and decoded by three NANDs into active-low lines for 00, 10 and 01
R2 comparator, match line: wired NOR of the eight XORs (h_eq_r2, high when R2 = c); load and exit in slice s1; leaves west in poly, then north on the bundle
data bits 0-3, east: the routing-zone rows on east to four contacts
carry gap 1: carry out of bits 0-6 leaves here, carry into bit 7 arrives; horizontal poly bands
clock gate row: six inverters: two pairs delay each clock phase for the other half of the generator; one pair sits across the two phase lines
R8 bit outputs west: two of five metals above R8's row, each under two slice rails in poly, to the gates
ck_a rail: clock phase A up the right edge of the mid-right array, one tap per row
middle bundle, lower part: T0 (strobe) ends; T1-T6 turn west; T7/T8 selects end at their gates; write strobes and buffered selects go on south
bus field below the island: VCC bus (y 4198-4250) and VSS bus (y 4288-4335) turning south; b, g, i arrive from tc2; l2_out, l3_out leave south and (l3_out) east; two through lines datapath to tc2
R9 compare lines, nest: five metals between two cross-unders
select buffers R16 R17 R15 R14: two inverters each; the buffered selects go down tracks T11-T14 (?read enables)

svg.text: select buffers R16 R17 R15 R14

rect.title: six north-south lines ns1-ns6: ns1 = island input w1 (from logic at the datapath slice-0 position); ns2 from the west bus; ns3, ns4, ns6 from over the datapath, ns3/ns4 on south to tc2; ns5, ns6 tap polys going east. No transistors
bit-0 XOR cells: two copies of the comparator's XOR cell: one makes the R9 comparator's bit-0 input, the other the row address bit-0 source
D0 pre-driver: d0_pu = NOR(d_hiz, d0_out_n), d0_pd = NOR(d_hiz, d0_pu): both output gates low while d_hiz is high (tri-state)
D1 pre-driver: d1_pu = NOR(d_hiz, d1_out_n), d1_pd = NOR(d_hiz, d1_pu): both output gates low while d_hiz is high (tri-state)
D2 pre-driver: d2_pu = NOR(d_hiz, d2_out_n), d2_pd = NOR(d_hiz, d2_pu): both output gates low while d_hiz is high (tri-state)
D3 pre-driver: d3_pu = NOR(d_hiz, d3_out_n), d3_pd = NOR(d_hiz, d3_pu): both output gates low while d_hiz is high (tri-state)
D4 pre-driver: d4_pu = NOR(d_hiz, d4_out_n), d4_pd = NOR(d_hiz, d4_pu): both output gates low while d_hiz is high (tri-state)
